nodes.name: Housekeeping - 03:20 daily
nodes.notes: After the judging window closes (04:00 local) and before the working day, so a report opened at 08:00 already carries last night's numbers.

nodes.name: Fetch Bitrix deals
nodes.notes: Was a direct crm.deal.list with start:0 and no paging, so it imported 50 of the 676 deals modified in a week -- every night, reporting success. Bitrix pages every list method at 50 and a short page is indistinguishable from a small result set. Paging is a loop with a stop condition, so it lives in the worker; this is one call. The response keeps Bitrix's own {result: [...]} shape, which is why the SQL below did not change.

parameters.query:
-- Bitrix deals, pulled instead of exported by hand.
--
-- WHAT THIS REPLACES. A human exported DEAL_*.csv from the CRM, copied it to a
-- laptop, opened a Railway tunnel and ran import_bitrix_phones.py. That is a
-- snapshot with a date on it: re-running it a month later knows nothing about
-- anything that happened since, and between exports every new conversation is
-- an island with no customer to belong to.
--
-- ONLY THE ALLOWLISTED FIELDS. The deal object carries UF_CRM_1781281581, which
-- contains prose addressed to a bot, and a dozen fields holding another
-- system's AI verdicts on lead temperature and intent -- the exact judgements
-- this project exists to produce from the conversation itself, with evidence.
-- Importing somebody else's unverifiable version of them puts two disagreeing
-- answers in one database with nothing to say which is which.
INSERT INTO deals (
  bitrix_deal_id, title, category_id, stage_id, stage_semantic, is_closed,
  amount, currency, created_at_src, modified_at_src, begin_date, close_date,
  origin, assigned_by_id, source_channel, bitrix_contact_id)
SELECT d->>'ID', d->>'TITLE', d->>'CATEGORY_ID', d->>'STAGE_ID',
       -- nullif: the CHECK allows 'P','S','F' and NULL. An absent
       -- STAGE_SEMANTIC_ID makes left('',1) = '', which is none of those and
       -- takes the whole batch down.
       nullif(left(coalesce(d->>'STAGE_SEMANTIC_ID', ''), 1), ''),
       -- coalesce: is_closed is NOT NULL DEFAULT false, but an EXPLICIT null
       -- in an INSERT column list overrides the default rather than falling
       -- back to it. NULL = 'Y' is NULL, so a missing CLOSED field failed
       -- every row -- which is exactly what happened.
       coalesce((d->>'CLOSED') = 'Y', false),
       nullif(d->>'OPPORTUNITY', '')::numeric,
       nullif(d->>'CURRENCY_ID', ''),
       nullif(d->>'DATE_CREATE', '')::timestamptz,
       nullif(d->>'DATE_MODIFY', '')::timestamptz,
       nullif(d->>'BEGINDATE', '')::date,
       nullif(d->>'CLOSEDATE', '')::date,
       -- 'bitrix', not 'bitrix_rest': deals_origin_ck (migration 015) allows
       -- exactly 'bitrix' and 'ai_derived', and every row of this pull failed
       -- the check. origin records WHO asserted the deal exists -- Bitrix did,
       -- whether it arrived by CSV or by REST -- so the existing value is the
       -- right one and no migration is needed on a live table.
       'bitrix',
       -- ASSIGNED_BY_ID has been in DEAL_SELECT since the allowlist was
       -- written; nothing ever read it, so `deals.agent_id` stayed NULL on
       -- every row and v_agent_scorecard -- which INNER JOINs agents on the
       -- evaluation's agent_id -- returned nothing at all. Storing the raw id
       -- here lets link_agent_attribution() (018) resolve it to our uuid, and
       -- lets a roster correction be replayed without re-pulling Bitrix.
       nullif(d->>'ASSIGNED_BY_ID', ''),
       -- SOURCE_ID has been in the allowlist and fetched all along, and was
       -- then dropped on the floor: `source_channel` had no writer, so no
       -- report could say which channel a deal came from. It is the only place
       -- that answer exists -- the chat API's own payload carries no channel
       -- field at all (verified: dealid, message, sender_id, timestamp,
       -- contact_id, created_at, updated_at, sender_role, content_type,
       -- crm_entity_id, conversation_id, and nothing else).
       nullif(d->>'SOURCE_ID', ''),
       -- CONTACT_ID was the third field fetched and discarded. Without it
       -- `deals.customer_id` had never held a value, so a customer's deals
       -- could only be reached through their CONVERSATIONS -- and a deal opened
       -- for someone who never chatted was invisible on their profile.
       -- link_deal_customers() (024) resolves this to our merged customer.
       nullif(d->>'CONTACT_ID', '')
FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS d
WHERE d->>'ID' IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (bitrix_deal_id) DO UPDATE SET
  title           = EXCLUDED.title,
  stage_id        = EXCLUDED.stage_id,
  stage_semantic  = EXCLUDED.stage_semantic,
  is_closed       = EXCLUDED.is_closed,
  -- NEVER overwrite an amount a human typed. is_manual_amount marks those, and
  -- the CRM's own number losing to it is the whole point of that flag.
  amount          = CASE WHEN deals.is_manual_amount THEN deals.amount
                         ELSE EXCLUDED.amount END,
  currency        = EXCLUDED.currency,
  modified_at_src = EXCLUDED.modified_at_src,
  close_date      = EXCLUDED.close_date,
  -- a deal genuinely changes hands; the CRM is the authority on who owns it.
  assigned_by_id  = coalesce(EXCLUDED.assigned_by_id, deals.assigned_by_id),
  source_channel  = coalesce(EXCLUDED.source_channel, deals.source_channel),
  -- coalesce, not a bare overwrite: a deal whose contact was later cleared in
  -- Bitrix must not lose the link we already resolved from it.
  bitrix_contact_id = coalesce(EXCLUDED.bitrix_contact_id, deals.bitrix_contact_id),
  updated_at      = now()
RETURNING deal_id, bitrix_deal_id, stage_id;

-- Link conversations to the deals that now exist, and nothing else.
--
-- 01c deliberately does not create a stub deal, so a thread that arrived before
-- its deal was pulled carries external_deal_id and a NULL FK. This closes that
-- gap once the deal is really there.
--
-- NEVER OVERWRITES: only rows where deal_id IS NULL are touched.
UPDATE interactions i
   SET deal_id = d.deal_id, updated_at = now()
  FROM deals d
 WHERE d.bitrix_deal_id = i.external_deal_id
   AND i.deal_id IS NULL
RETURNING i.interaction_id, d.bitrix_deal_id;

-- Retention. Raw customer words older than the window are deleted; every
-- conclusion drawn from them, and the id needed to fetch them again from
-- Bitrix or Drive, is kept forever.
--
-- CHAT AND CALL WINDOWS DIFFER ON PURPOSE. Bitrix still holds the chat text,
-- so 90 days is recoverable. A call recording is not reliably recoverable: if
-- Drive's own retention deletes the WAV after we deleted our transcript, that
-- conversation is gone from the world. Call text therefore keeps a year, which
-- costs 0.14 GB.
--
-- The rule lives in purge_raw_content (017), not here, so a backfill and this
-- node can never disagree about what "old" means.
SELECT * FROM purge_raw_content(90, 365, false);

-- Did anything actually get judged today, and what has it cost?
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. Chat threads were stored for six days without a single one
-- being evaluated and nobody noticed -- 01d was simply switched off. Storage
-- succeeding while scoring silently does nothing is the failure this pipeline
-- is most prone to, because every dashboard keeps rendering the older numbers
-- and looks healthy.
--
-- A row with detail->>'alert' = true is the signal. It is deliberately a ROW
-- and not an exception: a workflow that throws stops, and a nightly job that
-- stops is one more thing that fails quietly.
WITH last24 AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_evaluations WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS evaluations,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM chat_messages     WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS messages_in,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM transcripts       WHERE transcribed_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS transcripts_in,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM chat_eval_jobs    WHERE status IN ('pending','judge_failed')) AS queue,
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) FROM model_calls WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS spend_24h,
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) FROM model_calls WHERE created_at > date_trunc('month', now())) AS spend_month
)
INSERT INTO job_runs (job_name, started_at, finished_at, status, items_in, items_ok, cost_usd, detail)
SELECT 'nightly_health', now(), now(),
       -- CAST IS NOT OPTIONAL. job_runs.status is the job_status enum, and an
       -- unqualified CASE yields text: "column \"status\" is of type job_status
       -- but expression is of type text". Postgres casts a bare literal for you
       -- and refuses to cast a CASE, so this node was the only one in the
       -- workflow that could not run -- and it is the node that reports whether
       -- anything got judged at all.
       (CASE WHEN evaluations = 0 AND messages_in > 0 THEN 'failed' ELSE 'succeeded' END)::job_status,
       messages_in, evaluations, spend_month,
       jsonb_build_object(
         'evaluations_24h', evaluations,
         'messages_24h',    messages_in,
         'transcripts_24h', transcripts_in,
         'queue_depth',     queue,
         'spend_24h_usd',   spend_24h,
         'spend_month_usd', spend_month,
         -- The budget guard. Crossing it does not stop anything by itself; it
         -- puts a visible row in job_runs, which is what a human acts on.
         'over_budget',     spend_month > 40,
         'alert',           (evaluations = 0 AND messages_in > 0) OR spend_month > 40)
FROM last24
RETURNING run_id, job_name, status, detail;

-- Which contacts are we still missing something for?
--
-- WAS "missing a phone". A name is now the second thing we come here for
-- (027): crm.contact.list carries NAME/LAST_NAME and this is the only node
-- that ever asks Bitrix about a contact, so widening the question here is the
-- whole of the fix on the read side.
--
-- THREE REASONS TO ASK, AND THEY EXPIRE DIFFERENTLY.
--
--   no phone          identity resolution matches on E.164 and nothing else,
--                     so a conversation with no phone can never reach a
--                     customer. Retried every night; it is the expensive gap.
--   never fetched     we have never seen this contact's record at all.
--   fetched, no name  the CRM genuinely has no name on file. Retried MONTHLY,
--                     not nightly -- a contact that will never have a name
--                     would otherwise occupy the 500-id budget forever and
--                     starve the contacts that would answer.
--
-- Bounded on purpose. crm.contact.list takes a filter, not the whole address
-- book, and 500 distinct ids is more than a night's worth of new conversations.
-- Anything left over is picked up tomorrow.
--
-- DISTINCT MOVED INSIDE THE LIMIT. It used to take 500 ROWS and then dedupe
-- them, so a busy contact with 40 threads could spend 40 of the 500 places and
-- the batch would carry a couple of hundred real ids. 500 now means 500.
SELECT jsonb_agg(cid) AS contact_ids,
       count(cid)     AS n
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT i.external_contact_id AS cid
  FROM interactions i
  LEFT JOIN bitrix_contacts bc
         ON bc.bitrix_contact_id = i.external_contact_id
  WHERE i.external_contact_id IS NOT NULL
    AND i.external_contact_id <> ''
    AND (i.customer_phone_e164 IS NULL
         OR bc.bitrix_contact_id IS NULL
         OR (bc.full_name IS NULL
             AND bc.fetched_at < now() - interval '30 days'))
  LIMIT 500
) s;

nodes.name: Fetch Bitrix contacts
nodes.notes: Same paging bug one node later: filter {ID: [...500 ids]} is capped at 50 rows like everything else, so 450 contacts were dropped silently and their conversations kept a null phone -- which is exactly what stops workflow 03 creating a customer.

nodes.name: Normalise phones
nodes.notes: DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION=SA is a DECISION, not a format: 0500000000 is a valid Saudi mobile and meaningless in Egypt. A bare Egyptian number fails here rather than being assigned +966 — a null phone is recoverable, a wrong-country match merges two real people. The rule lives in the worker; this asks it instead of keeping a second copy in SQL.

parameters.query:
-- Write the normalised phone onto every conversation of that contact.
--
-- ZIPPED BY POSITION. The worker returns one result per value, in the order it
-- received them, so ordinality is the join key. That is only safe because the
-- pairing node builds both arrays in one pass -- if either list is ever built
-- separately, this join silently pairs the wrong phone with the wrong person.
--
-- NEVER OVERWRITES. Only rows where customer_phone_e164 IS NULL are touched: a
-- phone already there came from the source that owns the conversation, and a
-- nightly CRM sweep does not get to overrule it.
--
-- NULLS ARE SKIPPED, NOT WRITTEN. A number that failed to normalise (a bare
-- Egyptian mobile, say) leaves the row untouched and eligible tomorrow, rather
-- than being stamped with a wrong-country guess that would merge two people.
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT ordinality AS o, value->>'contact_id' AS cid
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(value, ordinality)
), norm AS (
  SELECT ordinality AS o, value->>'e164' AS e164
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(value, ordinality)
)
UPDATE interactions i
   SET customer_phone_e164 = n.e164,
       updated_at = now()
  FROM pairs p
  JOIN norm n ON n.o = p.o
 WHERE i.external_contact_id = p.cid
   AND i.customer_phone_e164 IS NULL
   AND n.e164 IS NOT NULL
RETURNING i.interaction_id, i.external_contact_id, i.customer_phone_e164;

-- The CRM's own answer about who this person is, stored instead of discarded.
--
-- WHY THIS NODE DID NOT EXIST. `Pair contact to phone` reads `c.PHONE` off each
-- contact object and drops the rest, so NAME and LAST_NAME arrived in this
-- workflow's memory every night and left it again. `customers.display_name` has
-- been NULL since 002 partly because of these four lines of JavaScript.
--
-- WHAT BITRIX SAID, NOT WHAT WE CONCLUDED. This table is the CRM's record.
-- `customers.display_name` is our conclusion, written by resolve_customer_names()
-- in workflow 03, which runs after identity resolution because it needs
-- customer_id. Keeping the two apart is what makes a wrong name auditable.
--
-- A NULL NEVER ERASES A STORED NAME. Every column coalesces onto what is
-- already there. If the select list on /bitrix/contacts is ever narrowed again,
-- the fields stop arriving and arrive as NULL rather than as an error (gotcha
-- 16) -- and the failure mode of that must be "we learn nothing new", never
-- "we forget what we knew".
INSERT INTO bitrix_contacts (bitrix_contact_id, name, second_name, last_name,
                             phone_raw, fetched_at)
SELECT c->>'ID',
       nullif(btrim(c->>'NAME'), ''),
       nullif(btrim(c->>'SECOND_NAME'), ''),
       nullif(btrim(c->>'LAST_NAME'), ''),
       nullif(btrim(c->'PHONE'->0->>'VALUE'), ''),
       now()
FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS c
WHERE nullif(btrim(coalesce(c->>'ID', '')), '') IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (bitrix_contact_id) DO UPDATE SET
  name        = coalesce(EXCLUDED.name,        bitrix_contacts.name),
  second_name = coalesce(EXCLUDED.second_name, bitrix_contacts.second_name),
  last_name   = coalesce(EXCLUDED.last_name,   bitrix_contacts.last_name),
  phone_raw   = coalesce(EXCLUDED.phone_raw,   bitrix_contacts.phone_raw),
  fetched_at  = now()
RETURNING bitrix_contact_id, full_name;
